head: claude/mi174-digest-generator-header-20260908
title: fix(ops): error-feed digest generator emits the doc-status header R3 requires
body:
MI-174 · `WO-20260908-THE-OPERATOR-S-ERROR-FEED-DIGEST-IS` · intent `IN-20260903-TRADING-SYSTEM-HEALTH` · cycle `CY-20260906-TRADING-TRUTH`
Backlog: `BL-20260908-ERROR-FEED-DIGEST-GENERATOR-STRIPS-THE-DOC-STATUS-HEADER-SO-EVERY-DIGEST-PR-IS-RED`

## The defect

`docs/claude/ERROR-FEED-DIGEST.md` is a REGISTERED document and is deliberately **not** on `document_index.GENERATED`'s waiver list, so `check_document_index.py` **R3** requires a `> **Doc status:**` header on it. `scripts/ops/error_feed_digest.py` rewrote the file wholesale and emitted none — so `main`'s copy (stamped by hand by a `document_index.py --write` run) passed while **every regenerated copy failed R3 UNSTAMPED**.

The consequence is why this is an integrity defect and not a formatting nit: **the workflow grades the FETCH, not the PR.** Every digest PR went RED on a required check while the run that opened it reported SUCCESS. The operator's error feed was **silently frozen** — it looked like it was being produced and was not landing. Three `automation/error-feed-digest-*` branches are stranded on the remote, which is MI-62's shape exactly ("automation commits, pushes, then fails to land — orphaned branches, nothing notices").

## Diagnosis verified before fixing, not taken on trust

Against the real artifact on `automation/error-feed-digest-34170995331-1`:

| tree | `check_document_index.py` |
|---|---|
| `main`'s stamped copy | `population=1007 registered=1007` · **OK** |
| that branch's actual digest content | **FAIL — 1 finding:** `R3 UNSTAMPED: docs/claude/ERROR-FEED-DIGEST.md` |

That branch's digest contains **zero** `Doc status:` lines; `main`'s contains one.

## The fix

The generator emits the stamp, **derived — never hardcoded**.

`document_index.stamp_for()` runs the *same computation that produces this file's ROW*, so the header and the row cannot disagree — which is the whole of what R3 checks. Hardcoding `unknown` would pass today and reintroduce the two-surfaces-two-answers drift the moment the row is ever assessed.

`assess()` is factored out of `build_rows` so both derive from one function. **Verified behaviour-preserving across all 1007 rows** — rows and rendered index byte-identical before/after. The derived stamp is byte-identical to the one on `main`.

The stamp is placed where `document_index._insert_at` would put it, so a later `--write` is a no-op rather than a second header. `doc_stamp()` **raises rather than writing an unstamped digest** — an undeliverable stamp is a broken runner, which this workflow's own header says is a valid failure, and failing loudly beats committing another digest that reds its own PR.

## Graded BY MUTATION — asserted, not assumed

Asserting the stamp is merely *present* would pass just as happily if R3 stopped caring — the guard-nobody-has-seen-fail problem. So both the module `--self-test` and pytest run **`check_document_index.evaluate`, the real rule engine**, over this generator's own rendered output, twice: as rendered, and with the stamp line deleted.

With `render_markdown` patched to drop the stamp:

```
self-test  -> exit 1: AssertionError: the rendered digest must satisfy R3:
              ['R3 UNSTAMPED: docs/claude/ERROR-FEED-DIGEST.md carries no status header...']
pytest     -> 5 failed, 21 passed
restored   -> 26 passed - self-test: 9 property groups (16 controls) OK
```

The inert-check compares line **counts**, not joined strings: `"\n".join(splitlines())` drops a trailing newline, so a string compare reads "changed" even when the mutation removed nothing — a control that passes vacuously. That flaw was in the first draft and was caught by *running* the mutation, not by reading it.

## End-to-end

A real `--write` against the live feeds (`verdict=all_feeds_read`, 122 groups, 1474 rows) emits the header, and `check_document_index.py` reports **OK**. Generated artifacts are deliberately **not** committed here — the proof that a regenerated digest lands is the workflow's own next PR, observed rather than asserted.

## What this does NOT do

**R3 is untouched. Nothing is added to any exclusion list.** Trading a frozen digest for an unregistered one is strictly worse — the guard exists so a document cannot enter the library without a status.

## Scope note

Beyond the stated Tier-1 scope (`error_feed_digest.py` + its test), this adds `assess()` / `stamp_for()` to `scripts/ops/document_index.py`. Composing the stamp otherwise needs three module-private helpers plus a copy of the `last_verified` rule — a second surface free to drift, which is the failure this register exists to end. It **strengthens** the single-authority property and weakens no guard. Flagged rather than smuggled.

The coordination board (#6927) is at GitHub's hard 2500-comment cap; writes 403 and reads return a board frozen at 2026-09-07T11:28:17Z. The mandatory START claim could not be posted. Known and parked.
